note_on_method: Two of the five filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Cape Coral. Free does, because the City states in one sentence that its park pickleball courts cost nothing. Lights does, because the City marks lighting venue by venue, and marks its absence too, which is what makes the marks trustworthy. Indoor and outdoor have no driver: the City never uses either word about the five published venues, and the one venue it does call indoor states no court count.

slots.why_this_filter:
Every pickleball court in Cape Coral is free, so this page holds the same five venues as the city page. Twenty courts at Camelot Park, Giuffrida Park, Jim Jeffers Park, Joe Stonis Park and Sands Park, none of which costs anything to play on.

What makes the page worth reading is how rare that sentence is. This directory records a price only when an operator publishes one, and most do not: across fifteen other cities, the great majority of venues carry no fee answer at all, because a parks department that has never charged for a court rarely thinks to write down that it is free. Cape Coral thought to. Its Park Sports/Games page states that the City's tennis and pickleball courts are "available for public use at no charge and open from sunrise to sunset (or later for locations with lighting)". That makes Cape Coral one of only seven cities on this whole site with a free court.

The same sentence tells you when free means available. Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis have lights and stay open until 9:00 p.m. daily. Giuffrida has no lights and closes at sunset, which the City states outright. Sands is unmarked either way.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Cape Coral states that it costs nothing to play. All five published venues qualify under the City's blanket sentence about its park tennis and pickleball courts, so nothing on the city page is excluded from this one.

What does not qualify is more interesting. Four Freedoms Park, the City's own indoor pickleball at 4818 Tarpon Court, is explicitly not free: "$5 per person (maximum of 4 players at a time) to reserve 2 hours of playtime".

The Courts is excluded from the whole site rather than just this page. The City lists it among the locations covered by that "no charge" sentence, with "32 dedicated pickleball courts and 12 tennis courts", and publishes no address for it at all. A venue this site cannot locate does not publish, whatever its price.

faqs.a: Yes, on the City's own statement: its park tennis and pickleball courts are "available for public use at no charge". This site does not describe a venue as free unless an operator publishes it, which is why only five cities here have a free page at all.
No. Four Freedoms Park charges $5 per person for two hours, up to four players. It does not appear on this site at all, because the City never states how many courts it has.

slots.why_this_filter:
Three Cape Coral venues have lights, and fourteen of the city's twenty courts are at them: four at Camelot Park, six at Jim Jeffers Park and four at Joe Stonis Park. All three stay open until 9:00 p.m. daily, and all three are free.

In south-west Florida that combination is close to the whole point. A court that closes at sunset is one you use before work or at the weekend. A lit court until nine is one you can use after a working day.

What makes this page trustworthy rather than merely populated is a venue that is not on it. The City states that Giuffrida Park has no lights, and an operator that writes the absence down when it is true is an operator whose positive marks mean something. It also means the one remaining silence is a real one. Sands Park is marked neither lit nor unlit, so its lighting is recorded as not stated and it is kept off this page.

Three venues confirmed lit, one confirmed unlit, one unknown. That is a better lighting record than most cities on this site can show; Seattle has a dataset field for it, Scottsdale's venues are all lit, and a handful of operators since have answered the question at every venue.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the City of Cape Coral states that its pickleball courts have lights. Three qualify. Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis each read "with lights" and then "open until 9:00 p.m. daily", so the claim is not merely that lamps exist but that the courts stay usable until nine.

Two venues do not qualify, for opposite reasons. Giuffrida Park is excluded because the City says it has no lights, which is a stated answer rather than a gap. Sands Park is excluded because the City says nothing at all about its lighting, and a silence is not promoted into a yes here.

One further venue would be on this page if it could be located. Gator Trails Park has "Two (2) dedicated pickleball courts with lights" in the City's words, but neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find "3628 Garden Blvd", the address the City publishes for it.

One caveat sits inside a qualifying venue. At Jim Jeffers Park the City's "with lights" attaches to the four courts on the convertible tennis slabs. The two warm-up courts it counts separately carry no lighting statement.

faqs.q: How late can I play under lights in Cape Coral?
faqs.a: Until 9:00 p.m., daily, at Camelot Park, Jim Jeffers Park and Joe Stonis Park. The City states the closing time in the same clause as the lighting.

faqs.q: Are all six courts at Jim Jeffers lit?
faqs.a: The City's "with lights" applies to the four courts on the convertible tennis slabs. It says nothing about the two warm-up courts it counts separately on the same line.
